subject: science
title: KS3 / Year 7-9 Science - Motion and Pressure
subtitle: Reading passages for KS3 physics motion and pressure.
description: Five KS3 reading passages with comprehension questions on speed, graphs, forces, pressure, fluids, buoyancy, and practical work.

data.sourcePassage: Motion means a change in position over time. To decide whether something is moving, compare its position with a reference point such as a wall, a start line, or a bus stop. Distance tells us how far an object travels, while time tells us how long the journey takes. Speed links these ideas because speed is distance travelled per unit time. A pupil walking 90 m in 60 s has a speed of 1.5 m/s. If an object travels equal distances in equal times, it is moving at constant speed. If it covers different distances in equal times, its speed is changing. At KS3, speed usually means how fast something moves; velocity is used later for speed in a particular direction.

questions.question: What is motion?
questions.modelAnswer: Motion is a change in position over time.

questions.question: Which equation calculates speed?
questions.modelAnswer: speed = distance / time

questions.question: Calculate the speed of a pupil who walks 90 m in 60 s.
questions.modelAnswer: The speed is 1.5 m/s because 90 divided by 60 equals 1.5.

questions.question: Why is a reference point useful when describing motion?
questions.modelAnswer: It gives something to compare position with, so you can tell whether the object has moved.

questions.question: Explain the difference between constant speed and changing speed.
questions.modelAnswer: Constant speed means equal distances are covered in equal times; changing speed means different distances are covered in equal times.

data.sourcePassage: A distance-time graph shows how far an object is from a starting point as time passes. Time usually belongs on the horizontal x-axis, and distance belongs on the vertical y-axis. A rising straight line means the object is moving away from the start at constant speed. A horizontal line means the object is stationary because the distance stays the same even though time continues. A steeper rising line means a greater speed, not a greater pressure. A line sloping down usually means the object is returning towards the starting point. Curved lines show changing speed: a curve becoming steeper shows acceleration, while a curve becoming less steep shows deceleration.

questions.question: Which axis usually shows time on a distance-time graph?
questions.modelAnswer: Time usually goes on the horizontal x-axis.

questions.question: What does a horizontal line on a distance-time graph show?
questions.modelAnswer: The object is stationary.

questions.question: What does a steeper rising line show?
questions.modelAnswer: It shows a greater speed because distance changes more each second.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to say a steeper distance-time graph means higher pressure?
questions.modelAnswer: A distance-time graph shows motion, so steepness represents speed. Pressure depends on force and area.

questions.question: How would you recognise acceleration on a distance-time graph?
questions.modelAnswer: A curved line becoming steeper shows acceleration because speed is increasing.

data.sourcePassage: A force is a push or pull measured in newtons. Contact forces, such as friction, air resistance, water resistance, normal reaction, and applied force, need objects or materials to touch. Non-contact forces, such as gravity and magnetism, can act without touching. Balanced forces are equal in size and opposite in direction, so they cause no change in motion. This can mean an object stays still or keeps moving at constant speed in a straight line. Unbalanced forces change motion by causing acceleration, deceleration, or a change in direction. During a parachute jump, weight is greater than air resistance at first, so the parachutist accelerates downwards. When the parachute opens, air resistance increases and the parachutist decelerates.

questions.question: What is a force?
questions.modelAnswer: A force is a push or pull.

questions.question: Which force is non-contact?
questions.modelAnswer: Gravity is a non-contact force.

questions.question: What can balanced forces do to an object moving in a straight line?
questions.modelAnswer: They can let it continue at constant speed because there is no change in motion.

questions.question: Why does a trolley accelerate if the pulling force is greater than friction?
questions.modelAnswer: The forces are unbalanced forwards, so the trolley speeds up in that direction.

questions.question: Explain why a parachutist slows down when the parachute opens.
questions.modelAnswer: The parachute greatly increases air resistance. Air resistance becomes larger than weight, so the forces cause deceleration.

data.sourcePassage: Pressure is force spread over an area and is calculated using pressure = force / area. The unit pascal is the same as one newton per square metre. If the same force acts over a smaller area, the pressure is higher. This explains why drawing pins, needles, and sharp knives work well: their tiny contact areas produce high pressure. Increasing the contact area lowers pressure when the force stays the same, so snowshoes, skis, wide tyres, and wide bag straps spread force out. Liquids and gases are fluids, and pressure in a fluid acts in all directions. Gas pressure happens when gas particles collide with surfaces. Liquid pressure increases with depth because deeper water has more water above it pressing down.

questions.question: What is the equation for pressure?
questions.modelAnswer: pressure = force / area

questions.question: What happens to pressure if the same force acts over a smaller area?
questions.modelAnswer: Pressure increases.

questions.question: Calculate the pressure when a 50 N force acts over 0.5 m2.
questions.modelAnswer: The pressure is 100 N/m2 or 100 Pa.

questions.question: Why is a wide bag strap more comfortable than a narrow strap?
questions.modelAnswer: It spreads the same force over a larger area, which lowers the pressure on the shoulder.

questions.question: Why are dam walls often thicker at the bottom?
questions.modelAnswer: Liquid pressure increases with depth, so the bottom of the dam must withstand greater water pressure.

data.sourcePassage: Floating and sinking depend on density, volume, displaced water, weight, and upthrust. Density means mass per unit volume. Upthrust is the upward force from a fluid. An object floats or stays at a steady depth when upthrust balances weight. It sinks when weight is greater than upthrust. A steel nail sinks because it is dense, small, and displaces only a small volume of water. A steel ship can float because its hollow shape gives it a large volume, it contains air, and it displaces enough water for upthrust to balance weight. Submarines change their average density using ballast tanks. Practical investigations test ideas fairly by changing one independent variable, measuring a dependent variable, and keeping control variables the same.

questions.question: What is upthrust?
questions.modelAnswer: Upthrust is the upward force from a fluid.

questions.question: When does an object sink?
questions.modelAnswer: It sinks when weight is greater than upthrust.
options: When weight is greater than upthrust
When time is on the x-axis
When force is spread over a larger area

questions.question: Why can a steel ship float even though a steel nail sinks?
questions.modelAnswer: The ship has a large hollow volume, contains air, and displaces enough water for upthrust to balance its weight.

questions.question: What happens when submarine ballast tanks fill with water?
questions.modelAnswer: The submarine mass and average density increase, so it is more likely to sink.

questions.question: In a pressure investigation using a block on clay, identify the independent and dependent variables.
questions.modelAnswer: The independent variable is contact area. The dependent variable is the depth of the mark in the clay.
